usages.explain: We will learn about demonstrative pronouns for location 「ここ／そこ／あそこ」. 「ここ」 indicates the location where the speaker is. 「そこ」 indicates the location where the listener is. 「あそこ」 indicates a location far from both the listener and the speaker. 「こちら／そちら／あちら」 are directional pronouns, but can also be used as polite alternatives to 「ここ／そこ／あそこ」.

examples.content: ここは ホテルです。
エレベーターはあそこです。
examples.transcription: えれべーたーはあそこです。

examples.content: トイレはどちらですか。 あちらです。
examples.transcription: といれはどちらですか。あちらです。
examples.mean: Where is the toilet? There it is.

usages.synopsis: ここ／そこ／あそこ／こちら／そちら／あちら are all positional pronouns.

usages.explain: Note: When the speaker considers that the listener is also within the range of their position, use 「ここ」to indicate a position slightly far from both, and use 「そこ」to indicate a position a bit farther away from both, and use 「あそこ」to indicate a relatively far position from both.

title: ここ／そこ／あそこ／こちら／そちら／あちら => here / there / over there
